newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Israelis appear in Cyprus court after escape bid.
newsitem.headline: Israelis appear in Cyprus court after escape bid.

text.p: Two Israelis who escaped from police detention in Cyprus on Wednesday appeared before a court on Friday and were ordered to stand trial on charges of possessing fake dollars next month.

Security was tight as Avi Biton and Shuki Samana -- who fled to the Turkish-held northern part of the island after their escape but were returned by Turkish Cypriot police -- appeared before a district court in the southern coastal town of Larnaca.
The court ordered Biton, 21, and Samana, 24, both from Haifa, to stand trial before the criminal court on October 15 on charges of possessing 72 forged $100 bills, discovered by police on August 30.

On Wednesday two motorcyclists in Nicosia blocked a police car taking Biton and Samana to the Larnaca court from prison, cut off their handcuffs and took them to a U.N. checkpoint at the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone, where all four ran to the Turkish Cypriot side.
Turkish Cypriot police returned Biton and Samana and the two motorcyclists -- Biton's brother David Biton, 24, and Amon Shimon, 28 -- the same day after U.N. intervention.
All four are being kept in a high security wing of the central prison in Nicosia.
On Thursday a court in Nicosia ordered that the four remain in custody for eight days pending inquiries into the escape.
